name: Harold Byrd
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember a packet of foreign coins taped to the pantry door.” On Monday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Harold knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I mailed a receipt for lunch. My family has been asking what an ordinary day costs.
appearance: Harold has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for close-cropped dark curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a red windbreaker with a pen clipped inside the neckline. In conversation Harold rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Harold has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Harold can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To explain the cost of an ordinary crew lunch at home.
family: Isabel Doyle is Harold’s cousin raised in the same household. Harold brings a spare shopping bag. Isabel chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A summer marriage*, Isabel says, “I have been saving for a huge wedding. Hearing these two haggle over chairs has made me question mine.”
connections: Selena Roberts. They send the night lights and the lunch receipt as two honest views from one shift.
